title: Choose the visual world
question: Four worlds for the same board. What you pick becomes the type, palette, density and one signature move that every surface inherits.

options.label: The Manifest
options.lineage: freight manifests and bills of lading
options.thesis: Every commitment is cargo: a docketed row, a stamped state, a carbon copy of what sits under it.
options.viewport: One board sheet: docket header, groups as holds, ruled rows, and the open item clipped to the right as a second sheet.
options.risk: A paper form without exact rules reads like a tax return.

raised.raise: Time has length, not just a date: a due window draws as a proportional bar against the week rule.
Registration furniture: every column rule, stamp and margin sits on one 4px baseline grid.
The active hold stays at full ink while the other holds recede one step behind it.

options.label: The Score Sheet
options.thesis: Long work kept the way a long game is kept: numbered turns, paired columns, annotations in red.
options.viewport: A padded sheet with week numbers in the margin, a heavy centre rule splitting the turn from its result, and the open item paper-clipped to the side.
options.risk: Chess notation can read as a game rather than a week's work.

options.label: The Concourse
options.thesis: The board answers “where next” the way a terminal does: one band per decision, distance stated in minutes.
options.viewport: Yellow sign bands over a warm grey board, arrows locked to the edge they point past, the detail panel reading as the gate.
options.risk: Reads as travel, not personal work, if the signage grammar loosens.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and sharpens navigation, but a solo week is not a concourse.

options.label: The Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The board as a proof sheet: a visible construction grid, rows snapped to its cells, one accent plane marking the open item.
options.viewport: A twelve-column hairline armature, the board snapped to its cells, and the open item taking the single blue plane.
options.risk: Grid-first becomes a specimen poster the moment the rows stop behaving like a table.
options.case: The clearest table of the four; the designer's specimen world fits this owner only partly.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.thesis: Rows are live departures: fixed character cells, one cascade when a state changes, date order enforced.
options.viewport: A matte black board of condensed caps in fixed cells, groups as concourse sections, amber marking what is late.
options.risk: A whole dark board is a costume unless the rows still edit like a table.
options.case: Rows and time map exactly onto the board, but the concourse is the wrong place for one person's week.

options.label: The Dance Score
options.thesis: Time runs upward on a central staff, duration drawn as the height of a block.
options.viewport: A vertical staff read from the bottom up, mirrored columns either side.
options.risk: Bottom-to-top time breaks every reading habit a task table has.
options.case: A working board cannot read upward; the idea survives only as bar length.
options.kept: Duration as length: the timeline bar grows with the work, not just the date.

options.label: The Plate Section
options.thesis: A near-white sheet with registration crosses, hairlines and a letterpressed stamp.
options.viewport: One continuous sheet of plates held by crosshair marks and a four-up hairline grid.
options.risk: An editorial plate world turns a working screen into a magazine page.
options.case: Beautiful and wrong here: the screen stops being a tool and becomes a page about one.
options.kept: Registration furniture: hairlines and crosshair marks holding the sheet to a baseline.

options.label: The Poster Wall
options.thesis: Rows of artwork where the focused tile expands to reveal its metadata and the rest dims.
options.viewport: Horizontally scrolling rows of poster tiles with a single accent border on focus.
options.risk: Tiles celebrate consumption; a board's rows are work to be finished.
options.case: The tile wall serves browsing, not triage, and the artwork is material the product does not have.
options.kept: Row-level dimming that leaves only the active group at full strength.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: A calm monochrome workspace with one accent, held to the finish of the best tool in this category.
canonCard.viewport: Left rail, one flat list of groups, status dots, a detail pane.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the tools you already use, by design.
